item.title: Refactor orders crate: order status String to OrderStatus enum
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, local socket): "The `orders` crate stores an order's status as a `String` and compares string literals all over the code. Refactor it to a proper type:

- Add `src/status.rs` with `pub enum OrderStatus { Pending, Paid, Shipped, Cancelled }` deriving at least `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash`.
- `OrderStatus::as_str(self) -> &'static str` returns the lowercase names ("pending", "paid", "shipped", "cancelled"); `Display` prints the same.
- `FromStr` for `OrderStatus` with `type Err = ParseStatusError`, a public error type that implements `std::error::Error` and whose message names the rejected input.
- `OrderStatus::can_transition_to(self, next: OrderStatus) -> bool` encodes the lifecycle: pending -> paid, pending -> cancelled, paid -> shipped, paid -> cancelled; nothing else.
- `Order::status` becomes an `OrderStatus`; re-export `OrderStatus` and `ParseStatusError` from the crate root; use the enum everywhere, so the status string literals appear only in `src/status.rs`.

Observable behaviour (errors, report output and ordering, parsing) must stay exactly the same, and `cargo test` must pass. Commit your work."

Constraints: behaviour must be preserved exactly; the only new behaviour is the API described above. Status string literals must appear only in src/status.rs. Functions stay under 60 lines and follow the repo's existing style. Commit as the configured git user with no tool or AI attribution in the commit message.

stages.summary:
Baseline and characterization for the orders crate OrderStatus refactor (attempt 1, no feedback to address).

STRUCTURAL GOAL: replace `Order::status: String` with `OrderStatus` enum (Pending, Paid, Shipped, Cancelled) in src/status.rs with as_str/Display/FromStr(ParseStatusError)/can_transition_to; re-export from crate root; status literals only in src/status.rs. Behaviour (errors, report output and ordering, parsing) must be unchanged.

COMMITS (branch archon/xygf2en0-refactor-orders-crate-order-status-strin, not pushed):
- Original baseline: b5bb60d (bench fixture). Production code is byte-identical to it (verified: no diff in src/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, tests/orders.rs).
- bf70cf7 test: characterize lifecycle refusals and their messages
- d74a9e4 test: characterize bulk queries and status count ordering
- edc00be test: characterize report line parsing and its errors (HEAD)
- Tree of HEAD: 42a11ec5e3e6223da8acc091a6134d4db09431dc. Worktree clean. Only new file: tests/characterization.rs (18 tests, additions only; existing tests/orders.rs untouched).

CHECKS (run in the item cargo target, `cargo` 1.98.1, all with --locked; no README/CI/Makefile/rustfmt.toml exists, so these are the only repo-discoverable checks):
- Before tests (baseline b5bb60d): `cargo test` exit 0, 3 passed (tests/orders.rs). `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` exit 0. `cargo build` exit 0. `cargo fmt --check` exit 1: pre-existing drift in src/billing.rs, src/order.rs, src/report.rs, src/shipping.rs, tests/orders.rs (not reformatted; out of scope).
- After tests (HEAD edc00be): `cargo test` exit 0: characterization 18 passed, orders 3 passed. clippy -D warnings exit 0, build exit 0. `cargo fmt --check` exit 1 (same 5 pre-existing files). New test file: `rustfmt --check` exit 0.

PUBLIC SURFACE (must stay the same unless noted):
- order::Order {pub id: u32, pub customer: String, pub total_cents: u64, pub status: String}. ALLOWED CHANGE: status type -> OrderStatus (explicit in brief). Derives Debug, Clone, PartialEq.
- Order::new(u32,&str,u64) -> status pending; Order::is_open(&self) -> bool (pending|paid); Order::cancel(&mut self) -> Result<(),String>: allowed from pending/paid; error "order {id} cannot be cancelled: it is {status}".
- billing::pay(&mut Order) -> Result<(),String>: only from pending, else "order {id} cannot be paid: it is {status}". billing::outstanding_cents(&[Order]) -> u64: sums total of pending only.
- shipping::ship(&mut Order) -> Result<(),String>: only from paid, else "order {id} cannot be shipped: it is {status}". shipping::ready_to_ship(&[Order]) -> Vec<u32>: ids of paid, input order.
- report::status_counts(&[Order]) -> Vec<(String,usize)>: sorted by status NAME (BTreeMap<String>), omits absent statuses. Return type may change to the enum (brief says "use the enum everywhere"), but output text and order must stay: cancelled, paid, pending, shipped.
- report::to_line(&Order) -> "id,customer,total_cents,status" (no escaping).
- report::from_line(&str) -> Result<Order,String>: trims the WHOLE line only; splits on every comma; checks in this order: field count ("expected 4 fields, got N"), id ("bad id {:?}: {e}"), total ("bad total {:?}: {e}"), status exact and case-sensitive ("unknown status {:?}"). Trailing comma gives 5 fields.
- crate root: pub use order::Order (ADD OrderStatus, ParseStatusError). Modules billing, order, report, shipping are pub.

PITFALLS FOR THE REFACTORER:
1. Do NOT derive PartialOrd/Ord in declaration order for OrderStatus: that would sort the report pending,paid,shipped,cancelled. The pinned output is alphabetical by name (cancelled,paid,pending,shipped). Test `status_counts_are_sorted_by_status_name_and_omit_absent_statuses` catches this.
2. from_line's unknown-status message must stay exactly `unknown status "<raw field>"` (Debug-quoted raw input). Do not replace it with ParseStatusError's Display unless the text is identical.
3. from_line status matching must stay exact: no trim per field, no case folding. " paid" and "PAID" are rejected.
4. Existing transitions already match the brief's lifecycle table (pay: pending->paid; ship: paid->shipped; cancel: pending/paid->cancelled). Do not add transition enforcement to from_line.
5. Literal rule: the brief says status literals only in src/status.rs. Existing tests/orders.rs and the new tests/characterization.rs contain expected text such as "pending". I read the rule as covering production src/, and the characterization tests deliberately use only public functions and text expectations, so they compile against either String or enum types. The verifier should decide if tests/ literals are acceptable.

COVERAGE: pinned. Pay/ship/cancel refusal and success for every state pair, including exact messages and no mutation on refusal; is_open for all four states; outstanding and ready_to_ship with mixed states, input order and empty input; status_counts ordering and omission; to_line for all four names; from_line round-trip, whitespace, case, empty customer, field counts, id/total parse errors (including overflow and empty), and check precedence.
KNOWN GAPS: FromStr, ParseStatusError, as_str, Display and can_transition_to are new API; they can't be characterized beyond what from_line/to_line already pin. The refactorer and verifier must check the lifecycle table and that ParseStatusError names the rejected input. Nothing about std error text beyond the cases listed is pinned. No services or background processes were started; nothing needs stopping. Nothing was pushed.

Status literals now appear only in src/status.rs under src/. Checks at the final tree cbff027846c368b6be07921402f672afe8ac9557: cargo test --locked passes (characterization 18/18, orders 3/3, unit 3/3); cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo build --locked pass. cargo fmt --check still fails only on pre-existing drift in tests/orders.rs, which I did not touch. Behaviour is preserved: error texts, report order (cancelled, paid, pending, shipped), and from_line precedence and messages are unchanged. Brief-authorized public changes: Order::status is now OrderStatus, and status_counts returns Vec<(OrderStatus, usize)>. No pre-existing tests were modified. Limits: tests/ files still contain literal status names as expected text; no services were started, so nothing needs stopping. Risk is high because of the public type change.

pr.body: Approach: new private module src/status.rs defines OrderStatus (Pending, Paid, Shipped, Cancelled) with as_str, Display, FromStr (ParseStatusError), and can_transition_to encoding pending->paid, pending->cancelled, paid->shipped, paid->cancelled. Order::status is OrderStatus. Order::transition_to (pub(crate)) holds the single transition check and error text used by pay, ship and cancel. from_line parses via FromStr; its unknown-status message is unchanged because ParseStatusError displays the raw input Debug-quoted. status_counts returns Vec<(OrderStatus, usize)> and keeps alphabetical-by-name ordering via a BTreeMap keyed by as_str. Key files: src/status.rs, src/order.rs, src/billing.rs, src/shipping.rs, src/report.rs, src/lib.rs. Rustfmt was applied to the four touched src files. Checks: cargo test --locked: characterization 18 passed, orders 3 passed, unit 3 passed. clippy -D warnings and build pass. Assumptions and limits: Order::status and status_counts return types changed as the brief allows. tests/orders.rs and tests/characterization.rs still contain literal expected text (not src). tests/orders.rs has pre-existing fmt drift, left untouched.
pr.summary: Order status is now a typed enum, not a String. before: status compared against string literals in billing, shipping, order and report. now: OrderStatus with as_str/Display/FromStr and can_transition_to; literals only in src/status.rs. Observable behaviour unchanged.
pr.title: Store order status as an OrderStatus enum instead of String

risk.why: Breaking public API change: Order.status type changes from String to OrderStatus and status_counts returns OrderStatus instead of String. Authorized by the brief and behaviour-preserving, pinned by 18 characterization tests and 3 unit tests. Cross-cutting type change across four modules. Rubric says API breaks and cross-cutting refactors are high, and when in doubt pick higher.

stages.summary:
Verified the OrderStatus refactor on archon/xygf2en0-refactor-orders-crate-order-status-strin (HEAD cbff027846c368b6be07921402f672afe8ac9557; commits 0b2640a and bdbc551 on top of edc00be). Worktree was clean before and after; nothing committed, pushed, or switched; no services started.

Executed checks (--locked, CARGO_TARGET_DIR in the item cache):
- cargo test --locked: exit 0. Unit 3/3, tests/characterization.rs 18/18, tests/orders.rs 3/3.
- cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings: exit 0 (after cargo clean -p orders to force a re-check).
- cargo build --locked: exit 0.
- cargo fmt --check: exit 1, only tests/orders.rs:40 (pre-existing, untouched). Baseline also exits 1 on five files; the refactor made four src files fmt-clean. rustfmt --check on tests/characterization.rs and src/status.rs: exit 0.
- Baseline reproduction: git archive b5bb60d into a scratch dir with characterization.rs copied from HEAD. cargo test --locked exit 0, 18/18 characterization pass against the original production code; clippy clean.

Tests examined: git diff b5bb60d...HEAD -- tests/orders.rs is empty. git diff edc00be HEAD -- tests is empty, so characterization is unchanged since its three commits. No pre-existing test was modified or removed.

Public surface and behaviour: a throwaway public-API probe (Display-based output) built against baseline and HEAD gave 76 identical lines (cmp, re-run in fresh target dirs). It covers pay/ship/cancel from all four states with messages and resulting state, is_open, outstanding_cents, ready_to_ship, status_counts (mixed, empty, single, all four), to_line, and about 45 from_line inputs (field counts, empty/sign/overflow id and total, case, whitespace, unicode, CRLF, check precedence). Debug rendering differs as expected from the allowed type change: baseline shows status: "paid", HEAD shows status: Paid. New API probed at HEAD: can_transition_to over all 16 pairs is exactly pending->paid, pending->cancelled, paid->shipped, paid->cancelled; as_str/Display/FromStr round-trip; ParseStatusError displays unknown status " PAID", implements std::error::Error, and is usable as Box<dyn Error>. Production status literals appear only in src/status.rs. Every function is under 60 lines.

Notes (non-blocking; details in structured findings): the fmt failure is pre-existing and untouched; status_counts' return type change and the Debug rendering follow from the allowed "use the enum everywhere" change and should be confirmed by the operator; the literal rule is read as production-only, so test fixtures keep literals; report.rs has incidental rustfmt reflow of untouched lines.

Process note: my first API probe run reused a binary from the Debug probe because both probe crates share the package name and target dir. I re-ran each probe in its own target dir and re-ran the comparison; results above are from the re-runs.

Cleanup: removed .verify-baseline and .verify-probe from the worktree; git status is empty. Cargo outputs remain only in the item cache, which Archon deletes.

Verdict: PASS. Nothing is left undone.
